newsitem.title: SPAIN: FOCUS - Telefonica to sustain first half.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Telefonica to sustain first half.

text.p: A 19.5 percent rise in first half net profit at Spain's Telefonica group is likely to be sustained over the full year, based on continued growth of income from mobile and basic telephony, analysts said on Friday.
Telefonica announced net profits for the six months to June of 71.89 billion pesetas ($574.7 million), up from 60.15 billion pesetas during the same period a year earlier.
"The results are pretty good. They're in line with (market) expectations," said Luis Prota, analyst at AB Asesores brokerage in Madrid.
In particular analysts highlighted buoyant operating income, which rose 12.3 percent to 954.93 billion pesetas.
Operating income was boosted by strong growth of both basic and mobile telephony, the firm said.
Basic telephony was the "main source of income, thanks to a greater number of minutes used per line," Telefonica said in a statement.
"I think this result can basically be maintained over the year. I'm forecasting a 17-18 percent rise in net profit for 1996," said Javier Borrachero, telecoms analyst at Banco Central Hispano.
Analysts said that Telefonica may decide not to reflect such high profits growth at the year-end, and could either provision or pass over to extraordinary results a proportion of income.

"Over the rest of the year, they'll try to be conservative. They can't really give (profit) figures which are much higher than these because they've got what may be difficult times coming up," said one telecoms analyst who requested anonymity.

He said that the liberalisation of the domestic telephony market, as well as the opening of the market to foreign competion --in principle due to take place before 1999-- could mean that Telefonica would be best advised to be cautious.
"When foreign competition arrives they may need something to fall back on," he said.
A progressive reduction in international call charges from Spain will also mean that revenues in that area will not be quite as brilliant in the second half, analysts said.
But further costs containment and expectations of a continued fall in interest rates in the second half should benefit the firm.
"They're containing their ordinary costs and controlling such areas as the size of the workforce, and this should continue to help," BCH's Borrachero said.
Analysts agreed that these factors should underpin the share price ahead of the expected placement of the government's remaining 21 percent tranche in 1997. ($1=125.1 Peseta)
